primary_correction_confirmed.claim: RemoteObjectStore::get_to_file already stages/verifies/fsyncs/renames, and old 157 binary passes the real Garage 8 MiB cold-read concurrency test
primary_correction_confirmed.evidence: src/storage/remote_objects.rs get_to_file writes .rootyard-object-<uuid> in the destination parent, caps size at expected_size, verifies sha256+size, sync_all(), renames to destination, fsyncs parent, removes temp on error; TempObject guard removes temp. source-ready.json records old binary sha256 157748a PASS on tests/lfs_hydration_concurrency.py (real Garage 127.0.0.1:19000 via loopback proxy, 2 backend GETs, both bodies 8388608 bytes sha256 9ad7ed07.., final mode 0o600 nlink 1, no staging leftovers).
primary_correction_confirmed.conclusion: Do NOT describe the storage delta as a truncation/short-body fix. No direct-truncate race exists at the oid path on the certified baseline.

caller_staging_assessment.classification: hardening (defensible), not required for data integrity
caller_staging_assessment.real_defect_removed: old code called get_to_file(final oid path) then chmod 0600 AFTER the rename, so between the callee rename and the chmod a concurrent verify_path_integrity_bounded sees mode != 0600 and returns false: a concurrent reader gets a spurious failure and/or a second full remote hydration, and the tenant-addressable path transiently carries the umask default mode (0644) for the object bytes
safety_review: rename-to-final happens before guard.disarm() with no intervening await, so no cancellation point exists between a verified rename and disarm; an armed guard only ever removes this request own random .tmp-<uuid>

any cancellation before the rename leaves at most a removed staging file (guard drop) and, if the spawn_blocking rename still runs, an ENOENT error nobody observes; unverified bytes can never reach the final path
deadline is checked inside both bounded hash loops and passed to get_to_file, so staging verify and final verify are deadline-bounded
staging verify enforces size, sha256==oid, mode==0600, nlink==1 with O_NOFOLLOW open; chmod is by path on a self-generated uuid name (no attacker-controllable name), minor stylistic only
caller_staging_assessment.cost: one extra full local SHA-256 pass per cold hydration (callee stream hash + staging hash + final verify_local_until hash = 3 digest passes, formerly 2), two extra spawn_blocking tasks; no second download and no byte copy because the callee rename target and the final path are in the same directory
caller_staging_assessment.gc_temp_interaction: .tmp-<uuid> exactly matches the pre-existing upload-staging convention (stream_to_staging_and_publish uses the same name and StagingFileGuard) and is swept by storage_lifecycle gitfs_stage_cleanup -> clean_staging, which deletes regular nlink==1 .tmp-<uuid> files in repo_lfs_dir older than policy.stage_age_seconds (default 3600). In-flight downloads advance mtime so only the post-completion window is exposed; if a sweep did hit a stalled staging file the hydration fails closed (rename ENOENT) with no unverified publish.
residual_gaps: clean_staging does NOT sweep .rootyard-object-<uuid>, so a kill/crash mid-download can leave an orphan temp that nothing reclaims (pre-existing, also affects backup hydration)
repo quota accounting (check_repo_quota/disk_bytes over repo_lfs_dir) transiently counts staging bytes (pre-existing)

the same post-rename chmod window still exists at src/backup/lfs_inventory.rs hydrate (get_to_file straight to the final oid path, then chmod), so the always-0600-at-final-path invariant holds only for the LFS read path; ci_checkouts mirror_prepare uses an unswept .ci-<uuid> stage

crlf_bug.status: CONFIRMED real server-side fail-open, not client-side artefact
crlf_bug.mechanism: old gate required the exact byte prefix version https://git-lfs.github.com/spec/v1 + LF; a CRLF pointer therefore hit continue and was treated as ordinary content, skipping object existence and size verification
crlf_bug.client_behaviour: git-lfs 3.6.1 --check exit 0 and --check --strict exit 2 on the CRLF fixture: Decode accepts CRLF (Go line scanning drops the trailing CR) while strict canonical re-encode fails, so git lfs clean passes the CRLF pointer bytes through verbatim and the raw pointer reaches the server
crlf_bug.empirical: source-ready.json records old binary (sha256 157748a) RED on tests/lfs_publication.py: direct Git push accepted crlf_missing, while missing/wrong_size/invalid were rejected in the same run
crlf_bug.fix: starts_lfs_pointer accepts LF or CRLF after the v1 version line before the bounded canonical parse; new code path applies it for every publication gate call site

normalizer_bounded_correction.observation: models::parse_pointer already tokenizes with str::lines(), which strips one trailing CR per line, so parse_pointer alone would accept the tested CRLF shapes once recognition is fixed; normalize_pointer_line_endings is therefore redundant for the tested forms
normalizer_bounded_correction.not_incorrect:
it is not a pure no-op: folding every CRLF also turns size 13
 style variants into a parseable line, i.e. it accepts a slightly wider pointer-shape set than parse_pointer alone. The consequence is only fail-closed over-rejection (a shape is then forced through object availability/digest verification), never a bypass
normalizer_bounded_correction.bounds: allocation is bounded by MAX_POINTER_BYTES (1024) per blob and the batch by MAX_SMALL_BLOBS (4096), and normalization runs only on pointer-recognised blobs so ordinary text is untouched; canonical LF pointers contain no CRLF sequence, so no false rejection of previously valid LF pointers
normalizer_bounded_correction.out_of_delta: the impl worker is currently expanding the pointer normalizer (leading whitespace, legacy URI) in a later delta; those shapes are NOT accepted by 869be7d and require a separate narrow follow-up review

publication_test_material.covered: 7 pointer kinds (missing, wrong_size, invalid, crlf_missing, crlf_wrong_size, ready_missing_bytes, ready_corrupt_bytes) x 4 asserted paths (direct smart-HTTP push, --atomic push with a good ref that must also not move, ref transaction 409, pull/merge 409), each with ref-not-visible ls-remote assertions and object-byte hold/corrupt/restore; plus a valid CRLF pointer that must publish and must appear at the pushed head
bounded_gaps: no assertion that the committed Git blob bytes equal the CRLF pointer (cat-file -p), so the suite itself does not pin the client pass-through premise that explains the RED

parse_pointer ignores unrecognised lines, so the ready_* kinds do reach availability/ensure_readable (intended path); the crlf_* kinds are rejected as size/unavailable but the suite does not distinguish which guard fired
